story.what_it_does: ICICI Bank is an Indian bank that takes deposits and makes loans, earning mainly from the gap between the interest it charges and pays. In FY2026 its loans grew 15.8% and deposits 11.4%, with profit after tax of ₹501.47 billion.
story.plans: Management expects net interest margin to be range-bound in FY27 but gave no loan growth target. It also expects an update on the agri standard asset provision and deployment of excess liquidity within two quarters, and aims for carbon neutrality on Scope 1 and 2 emissions by fiscal 2032.
story.moat: The notes do not describe a competitive moat directly. Evidence of strength includes low bad loans (net NPA 0.30% in Sep-26), capital adequacy of 16.68% and a net interest margin above 4%.

scenarios.story: Loan growth accelerated to 30.0% by Sep-26 and profit rose 20.1%, while net NPA kept falling. If this holds with strong capital, earnings could keep growing.
signals_to_watch: Total loan growth year on year (30.0% in Sep-26)

scenarios.story: Profit grew steadily and asset quality stayed stable, with margin expected to be range-bound in FY27. Management calls the recent margin dip optical, with only moderate deposit repricing expected.
signals_to_watch: Net interest margin (4.18% in Q2 FY27 versus 4.36% in Q1)
Cost of deposits (4.50% in Q2 FY27)

scenarios.story: Margin fell from 4.36% to 4.18% and treasury income turned negative, while the RBI-directed agri provision remains unresolved. The West Asia conflict and a shrinking credit card book add uncertainty to growth and asset quality.
signals_to_watch: Update on the agri standard asset provision (₹12.83 bn made so far)
Credit card portfolio decline (9.7% year on year in Sep-26)
